Subject: Post-call recap: tool/function-calling patterns + next steps

Thanks again for taking the time this morning — great discussion. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps so we have alignment:

Summary / goals
- Objective: Integrate Redwood to power FinApps' intelligent assistant for transaction categorization and contextual suggestions.
- Primary concerns raised: auth & data routing, deterministic structured outputs for downstream systems, embeddings-based retrieval/reranking, and safe tool execution.

Technical patterns we discussed
- SDK + auth: use our server-side SDK with short-lived bearer tokens for your backend service; we recommend using customer-managed KMS for secrets in Prod.
- Routing: route high-priority autopay and fraud-check traces to dedicated capacity (Committed instances) and fall back to hosted lower-cost model for general suggestions.
- Tool calling: model returns structured tool-calls (JSON schema) + tool_id mapping in your orchestration layer. We recommend a hybrid approach: core transactional tools (balance lookup, post-transaction tagging) run synchronously; heavier ops (batch enrichment, ledger reconciliation) invoked asynchronously.
- Embeddings + reranker: low-latency vector store (we integrate with your existing Redis/FAISS layer) for candidate retrieval and a lightweight reranker model at serving time to improve precision on top-N.

Attachments: redwood-tool-calling-patterns.pdf (patterns + sample schemas)

Proposed next steps
1) I'll share a short MVP plan and a sample tool schema for your transaction-tagging flow (attached).
2) Tech deep-dive with your infra lead to confirm auth/KMS and routing (can we schedule for next week?).
3) POC scope: 4-week POC for tagging + embeddings-based search with SLA baseline and cost estimate.

Please reply here with availability and any questions.

	64
Marissa Cole

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: tool/function-calling patterns + next steps

Great questions — answering inline and adding some concrete implementation guidance:

On auth / tokens
- Our server-side SDK accepts bearer tokens issued by any external identity provider. Pattern: your backend exchanges a Vault-signed service token for a short-lived Redwood token via our token-exchange endpoint. This avoids embedding long-lived keys in your service.
- We also support mTLS for private deployments if you prefer mutual TLS rather than bearer tokens.

On tool execution semantics
- Recommended pattern: model emits a tool_call object with fields {tool_id, args, request_id, idempotency_key}. Your orchestration service acknowledges the tool call to Redwood with a tool_execution.status (started/failed/succeeded) via our events API.
- For at-least-once semantics, we advise designing tools to be idempotent (idempotency_key) and include a dedupe layer in your processing queue. Redwood can persist a mapping of request_id -> tool_call outcome for the duration of the POC if you want us to help with dedupe.

On reranker latency
- If you use a compact reranker (distilled cross-encoder) hosted on Dedicated capacity colocated with the vector store, we can typically hit ~30-50ms p99 for a top-10 rerank. Tradeoffs: higher-accuracy rerankers increase inference cost and memory footprint; we can provide a baseline model profile.

Suggested tool definitions (MVP)
- tag_transaction (sync): input {transaction_id, text, metadata} -> output {tags: [string], confidence: float, structured_reasoning: {category_id}}
- fetch_account (sync): input {account_id} -> output {balance, last_txn_id}
- enqueue_enrichment (async): input {batch_id, transactions[]} -> output {accepted: bool, queue_id}

Error handling recommendations
- Tool errors: return structured error codes (TEMPORARY, PERMANENT, RETRYABLE_WITH_BACKOFF) in the tool_execution response.
- Fallbacks: if a required sync tool fails, return a structured fallback response to the user and enqueue the operation for async retry with a compensating action.
- Monitoring: instrument per-tool success/failure rates and SLO alerts in Redwood Console.

Next steps (concrete)
1) I'll drop a short MVP doc and sample schema (attached).
2) Marcus, Rafael — can you join a tech deep-dive Tue 2026-10-20 10:00 AM PT? We expect 45m.
3) Tom / Elena — confirm if Vault-token exchange works for you or if you prefer mTLS.
